title: A principal localization of a global complete intersection over a field is a global complete intersection
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $T$ a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $g\in T$ and let $T_g$ be the localization of $T$ at the multiplicative set $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], a $k$-algebra through $k\to T\to T_g$. Then $T_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

proof.text: If the localization is the zero ring, use the zero-ring clause. Otherwise the localization map makes T nonzero. Extract n, c, f, c ≤ n, a k-algebra equivalence e from the polynomial quotient A to T, and dim T = n-c. The equivalence makes A nonzero. Transport Mathlib Algebra.Presentation.naive along e to obtain a presentation P of T with Fin n variables and Fin c relations.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SA (lemma-localize-lci), lines 35868-35876; Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35817-35831

proof.text: The composite of the principal localization spectrum map and the inverse spectrum homeomorphism induced by e is an open embedding j: Spec(T_g) → Spec(A). Transfer dim T = n-c to A by the homeomorphism. Equidimensionality gives dim_x Spec(A) = n-c at every point. The embedding identifies dim Spec(T_g) with dim(range j). The subspace bound gives dim(range j) ≤ n-c. Since T_g is nonzero, choose x in its spectrum. The open range of j is a neighborhood of j(x), so the infimum defining dimension at j(x) gives n-c ≤ dim(range j). The two bounds give dim T_g = n-c without a supremum-of-local-dimensions theorem or transport of local dimension.

proof.text: Compose P with Mathlib Algebra.Presentation.localizationAway for T_g over T. Algebra.Presentation.comp supplies a presentation with Unit ⊕ Fin n variables and Unit ⊕ Fin c relations, using the coefficient-kernel and localization polynomial quotient calculations in its existing proof. Reindex these types to Fin(n+1) and Fin(c+1) using cardinality equivalences. Algebra.Presentation.quotientEquiv, restricted to k-scalars, identifies the quotient by the span of the resulting relations with T_g. This replaces the handwritten kernel calculation with the existing Mathlib presentation API.
